fix: OopsError.Is() now compares by identity, not by type (#105)

Previously, Is() returned true for any OopsError target, making
errors.Is(errA, errB) true even for two unrelated OopsErrors. This
conflates type matching (the job of errors.As) with value matching
(the job of errors.Is).

OopsError contains non-comparable fields (maps, slices), so the default
== path in errors.Is would panic. Identity is now established via the
span ID, which is assigned uniquely per error at creation time.

Adds a regression test covering the broken case.

fix(trace): explicit Trace() always beats auto-generated trace (#106)

* fix(trace): explicit Trace() always beats auto-generated trace

Add traceAutoGenerated bool field to OopsError to distinguish library-
assigned traces from caller-set ones. Replace getDeepestErrorAttribute
for trace with getTraceFromChain, which walks the error chain and always
returns the deepest explicit trace, falling back to deepest auto-generated.

This fixes the precedence bug where:
  err := oops.Errorf("inner")            // auto trace
  err = oops.Trace("my-id").Wrap(err)   // explicit trace
  err.(OopsError).Trace()               // was returning auto trace

feature/caller skip (#109)

* feat: add CallerSkip and FrameSkip for stack trace control

CallerSkip(n) skips N additional frames when capturing the stack trace,
useful when oops.Wrap is called from helper functions. FrameSkip(file, fun)
registers a global frame filter using exact matching that excludes matching
frames from all stack traces.

Closes #65

* docs: add README docs for CallerSkip and FrameSkip; fix FrameSkip matching to use strings.Contains

* fix: FrameSkip uses exact equality for file path and short function name

File path is matched against the cleaned/shortened path. Function name is
matched against the short name (e.g., "Wrap" not "github.com/samber/oops.Wrap").
An empty string acts as a wildcard.

* test: add tests for CallerSkip and FrameSkip

* fix: CallerSkip(1) now skips 1 user frame; guard negatives; FrameSkip idempotent

* refactor: move FrameSkip filtering from capture-time to output-time

Store raw runtime.CallersFrames values (rawFile, rawFunction) on each
frame and apply framesSkip patterns lazily in Stacktrace(), Sources(),
and StackFrames() via applyFrameSkip(). Patterns registered after error
creation now also filter those errors stack traces.

* refactor: move FrameSkip filtering from capture-time to output-time

Filtering is now applied when Stacktrace(), Sources(), or StackFrames()
is called, not when the error is created. This means FrameSkip patterns
registered after error creation still apply to existing errors.

Also stores rawFile/rawFunction in oopsStacktraceFrame so matching uses
the raw runtime.CallersFrames values (strings.Contains) while display
continues using the cleaned/short forms.

* perf: cache Stacktrace() and Sources() output via sync.Once

Both methods share a single recursive frame traversal. Source fragment
computation (file I/O) is deferred until Sources() is first called.

refactor(builder): migrate to functional options pattern (linked-list optionFunc) (#121)

* refactor(builder): switch to linked-list optionFunc (fix fan-out bug)

Replace the builder with an immutable linked list:
  type optionFunc func(e *OopsError, next optionFunc)

Each method captures prev=b.head in a new closure; materialize() calls
b.head(e, nil) once to traverse the chain in forward order (prev first,
then self -- last-writer-wins for scalar fields, additive for maps/tags).

Fixes a correctness bug in the slice approach: when the same base builder
was materialized twice (fan-out pattern), snap maps were directly assigned
to e.context on nil-check, causing two OopsError instances to share the
same mutable map. Now snap is always merged via range loop, never
direct-assigned; each materialization allocates its own map.

Performance vs original builder (allocs/op, 0% variance):
  depth=4:      35 -> 18  (-49%)
  depth=7:      53 -> 19  (-64%)
  WithContext:  50 -> 21  (-58%)
  B/op depth=7: 4.9Ki -> 2.7Ki (-45%)

The linked list is O(1) per chained call vs O(N) slice-clone in the
previous implementation: depth=1 through depth=4 all land at 18 allocs
(closures stack-allocated by the compiler when they do not escape).

perf: single-pass chain traversal in LogValue/ToMap/formatVerbose (#124)

* perf: single-pass chain traversal in LogValue/ToMap/formatVerbose

Add snapshot(OopsError) OopsError that walks the error chain once,
collecting and merging all attributes (scalars, tags, maps). The three
hot-path rendering methods — LogValue, ToMap, formatVerbose — call
snapshot() at entry and read fields directly, reducing chain traversals
from O(n×h) to O(h) per render call.

Also extract mergeMaps() from mergeNestedErrorMap() so the merge logic
is shared between the existing public accessors and snapshot().

Results on a 1-level chain: -46% bytes/op, -14 allocs/op on ToMap and
LogValue. Gains scale with chain depth.

perf(helpers): fast-path type assertion in AsOops before errors.As (#134)

errors.As is reflection-based and AsOops is called once per layer by
every chain-traversal helper (recursive, getDeepestErrorAttribute,
collectMaps). When the wrapped error is directly an OopsError - the
common case in oops chains - a plain type assertion answers in ~1ns.
errors.As remains as fallback for chains interleaved with non-oops
wrappers (fmt.Errorf %w, custom Unwrap types).

benchstat vs main (darwin/arm64, Apple M3, -count=6 -cpu=1):

                │      sec/op      │   sec/op     vs base               │
ChainTraversal        1611.5n ± 1%   870.1n ± 0%  -46.01% (p=0.002 n=6)
ErrorDeepChain         46.47n ± 5%   46.62n ± 6%        ~ (p=0.699 n=6)
ReflectionPaths        514.3n ± 2%   533.9n ± 1%   +3.81% (p=0.002 n=6)
geomean                337.7n        278.7n       -17.46%

                │ before.bench.txt │            after.bench.txt            │
                │       B/op       │     B/op      vs base                 │
ChainTraversal      3.922Ki ± 0%     1.422Ki ± 0%  -63.75% (p=0.002 n=6)

                │ before.bench.txt │           after.bench.txt           │
                │    allocs/op     │ allocs/op   vs base                 │
ChainTraversal       14.000 ± 0%     6.000 ± 0%  -57.14% (p=0.002 n=6)

Note: BenchmarkReflectionPaths shows a stable ~4% time delta with
unchanged allocations even though it does not execute AsOops in its
timed loop - consistent with a binary layout artifact rather than a
logical regression.

perf(stacktrace): defer frame symbolization to first read 🔥 😍😍😍 (#137)

* perf(stacktrace): defer frame symbolization to first read

Program counters are still captured eagerly at error-creation time via
runtime.Callers (the stack is gone afterwards, so this cannot move), but
resolving PCs into file/function/line strings through
runtime.CallersFrames — the dominant cost of error creation per CPU
profile (~30% of BenchmarkNew) — now happens behind a sync.Once on
first access to Stacktrace()/Sources()/StackFrames().

Most errors in production are created, checked against nil, and
discarded without ever being formatted (BenchmarkBuilderCreatedNotRead
models this), so they no longer pay for symbolization at all. Errors
that are formatted pay the same total cost as before, on first read.

Filtering rules, their inputs (StackTraceMaxDepth is snapshotted at
capture time) and output are unchanged. GOROOT and the examples-package
prefix are now computed once at init instead of per error —
runtime.GOROOT re-reads an env var on every call.

This implements the existing "@TODO: filtering should be done lazily,
not at creation time".

perf(kv): skip merge of absent context/user/tenant maps in snapshot (#138)

mergeMaps allocates a fresh map even for empty input, so every
snapshot() paid up to three map allocations for fields the error
chain never set. Consumers only ever check len() on these fields, so
leaving them nil is equivalent; ToMap's in-place "id" insertion now
guards against the nil case explicitly.

perf(error): check SourceFragmentsHidden before formatting sources (#139)

* perf(error): check SourceFragmentsHidden before formatting sources

ToMap, LogValue and formatVerbose evaluated the condition

    if sources := o.Sources(); sources != "" && !SourceFragmentsHidden

left-to-right: Sources() formatted the full source-fragment output -
reading source files from disk and building per-line strings - and the
result was then discarded, because SourceFragmentsHidden is true by
default. Checking the flag first skips all of that work in the default
configuration; behavior with SourceFragmentsHidden=false is unchanged.

Also replaces fmt.Sprintf with direct concatenation in the per-line /
per-block builders (getSourceFromFrame, framesToStacktraceBlocks,
framesToSourceBlocks), benefiting the non-hidden path too.

* test(error): cover the SourceFragmentsHidden=false path

The previous commit gated Sources() behind SourceFragmentsHidden in
ToMap, LogValue and formatVerbose, but no existing test ever set
SourceFragmentsHidden=false, leaving oopsStacktrace.Source() and
framesToSourceBlocks at 0% coverage and the new gated branches
partially untested.

Adds:
- TestOopsSourceFragmentsVisible / TestOopsSourceFragmentsHiddenByDefault:
  verify ToMap, LogValue and formatVerbose include/omit "sources"
  depending on the flag.
- TestOopsStacktraceSource: direct coverage of oopsStacktrace.Source().
- TestFramesToSourceBlocks: direct coverage of framesToSourceBlocks,
  including the no-body-skips-block and multi-block-reversal cases.

Coverage: 90.8% -> 94.0%.

* test(error): run SourceFragmentsHidden tests sequentially

TestOopsSourceFragmentsHiddenByDefault asserts on the package-level
SourceFragmentsHidden default, which TestOopsSourceFragmentsVisible
temporarily flips. Both must run outside the parallel pool so the
flip-and-restore in the latter cannot interleave with the former
assumption; add the paralleltest lint suppression that comes with
opting out of t.Parallel() for that reason.
